s1.syndrome_frame: febrile neutropenic patient with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and multiple hypoattenuating liver and spleen lesions
salient_findings: multiple hypoattenuating lesions in the liver and spleen on CT scan
key_facts: history of perianal abscess during induction chemotherapy
currently undergoing maintenance chemotherapy with idarubicin and cytarabine
tachycardia with heart rate of 109 beats/min
percussion tenderness in the right upper quadrant
arthroconidia and hyphal fungi on Gram staining

raw.syndrome_frame: febrile neutropenic patient with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and multiple hypoattenuating liver and spleen lesions
salient_findings: multiple hypoattenuating lesions in the liver and spleen on CT scan
key_facts: history of perianal abscess during induction chemotherapy
currently undergoing maintenance chemotherapy with idarubicin and cytarabine
tachycardia with heart rate of 109 beats/min
percussion tenderness in the right upper quadrant
arthroconidia and hyphal fungi on Gram staining

shortlist.label: Hepatosplenic Candidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive blood cultures for yeast, arthroconidia and hyphal fungi on Gram staining, and multiple hypoattenuating liver and spleen lesions

shortlist.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, tachycardia, and percussion tenderness in the right upper quadrant, although less likely given the yeast-positive blood cultures

shortlist.label: Chronic Disseminated Candidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of acute promyelocytic leukemia, neutropenia, and evidence of fungal infection

shortlist.label: Fungal liver abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated liver enzymes, multiple hypoattenuating liver lesions, and positive blood cultures for yeast

shortlist.label: Candida krusei infection
shortlist.why_kept: Neutropenia, fever, and evidence of fungal infection, with Candida krusei being a possible cause of hepatosplenic candidiasis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and percussion tenderness, along with imaging studies showing multiple hypoattenuating lesions in the liver and spleen, and positive blood cultures for yeast, are consistent with Hepatosplenic Candidiasis, particularly in an immunocompromised patient with a history of chemotherapy.

rejected.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
rejected.why: While the patient is immunocompromised and has fever and respiratory symptoms, the presence of yeast in blood cultures and the specific imaging findings are more suggestive of candidiasis than aspergillosis.

rejected.label: Chronic Disseminated Candidiasis
rejected.why: This condition is a possibility but the term Hepatosplenic Candidiasis more specifically describes the involvement of the liver and spleen as seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Fungal liver abscess
rejected.why: The patient has multiple lesions in the liver and spleen, not just a single abscess, making Hepatosplenic Candidiasis a more accurate diagnosis.

rejected.label: Candida krusei infection
rejected.why: While the patient has a Candida infection, the species is not specified as Candida krusei, and the diagnosis of Hepatosplenic Candidiasis encompasses the infection without specifying the species.
